import pytest
from rich.console import Console
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

def test_isatty_proxy_attribute_error():
    # Mock a file object that has 'isatty' attribute, but calling it raises AttributeError
    # This simulates a proxy that proxies the attribute but fails on the call
    mock_file = MagicMock()
    mock_file.isatty = MagicMock(side_effect=AttributeError("Proxy error"))
    
    console = Console(file=mock_file)
    # This should not raise AttributeError thanks to the fix
    assert console.is_terminal is False

def test_isatty_none():
    mock_file = MagicMock(spec=[]) # No isatty attribute
    console = Console(file=mock_file)
    assert console.is_terminal is False

def test_isatty_true():
    mock_file = MagicMock()
    mock_file.isatty.return_value = True
    console = Console(file=mock_file)
    assert console.is_terminal is True

def test_isatty_false():
    mock_file = MagicMock()
    mock_file.isatty.return_value = False
    console = Console(file=mock_file)
    assert console.is_terminal is False

The fix was applied to `rich/console.py` by adding `AttributeError` to the exception handler when calling `isatty()`, ensuring that proxy objects that fail to correctly implement the method do not cause the application to crash. I verified that existing tests in `tests/test_console.py` still pass.

The `is_terminal` property in `Console` now handles `AttributeError` in addition to `ValueError`, returning `False` if either occurs during the `isatty()` call.
